154775.title: Total Qty sort puts untracked parts below tracked parts both ways
154775.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have five parts, part A, part B, part C, part D and part E, each with one bin location that holds a quantity above 0 (no bin below zero), so the sort and the Total Qty cells agree.
  • Set parts A, B and C as tracked parts, with 5, 5 and 2 on hand.
  • Set parts D and E as untracked parts, with 1 and 9 on their shelf.
  • Give parts A, B, C, D and E descriptions that start with the same text and end, in turn, with ALPHA, BRAVO, CHARLIE, XRAY and YANKEE.
  • Give parts A, B, C, D and E part numbers that start with the same text, so one search lists all five.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Active tab.

Setup

  1. Create the five parts as below, one at a time.
  2. Make part A: Click Parts in the top bar, Inventory in the left menu, then New Inventory Part. Fill in: Description: ZZAUTOTEST PL C154775 PART A ALPHA; Part Number: ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C154775-A; Category: any one; Cost: 10.00; Sell Price: 20.00; Quantity (in the bin row): 5. Click Save.
  3. Make part B: Click Parts in the top bar, Inventory in the left menu, then New Inventory Part. Fill in: Description: ZZAUTOTEST PL C154775 PART B BRAVO; Part Number: ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C154775-B; Category: any one; Cost: 10.00; Sell Price: 20.00; Quantity (in the bin row): 5. Click Save.
  4. Make part C: Click Parts in the top bar, Inventory in the left menu, then New Inventory Part. Fill in: Description: ZZAUTOTEST PL C154775 PART C CHARLIE; Part Number: ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C154775-C; Category: any one; Cost: 10.00; Sell Price: 20.00; Quantity (in the bin row): 2. Click Save.
  5. Make part D: Click Parts in the top bar, Inventory in the left menu, then New Inventory Part. Fill in: Description: ZZAUTOTEST PL C154775 PART D XRAY; Part Number: ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C154775-D; Category: any one; Cost: 10.00; Sell Price: 20.00; Quantity (in the bin row): 1. Click Track quantities and cost of goods off. Click Save.
  6. Make part E: Click Parts in the top bar, Inventory in the left menu, then New Inventory Part. Fill in: Description: ZZAUTOTEST PL C154775 PART E YANKEE; Part Number: ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C154775-E; Category: any one; Cost: 10.00; Sell Price: 20.00; Quantity (in the bin row): 9. Click Track quantities and cost of goods off. Click Save.
  7. The descriptions above all start ZZAUTOTEST PL C154775 PART.
  8. The part numbers above all start ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C154775-.
154775.custom_steps:
1. Type the shared start of the part numbers in the Search box.
  2. Click the Total Qty column header.
  3. Click the Total Qty column header again.
154775.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Parts A, B, C, D and E are listed.

Step 2:

  • The Total Qty header shows a sort arrow.
  • Low to high, the rows read part C (2), part A (5), part B (5), part D, part E; high to low they read part A (5), part B (5), part C (2), part D, part E. One of these two orders shows.
  • Parts A and B have the same quantity, so part A (ALPHA) comes before part B (BRAVO).
  • The untracked parts D and E sit below every tracked part, part D (XRAY) before part E (YANKEE), even though part E has 9 on its shelf.

Step 3:

  • The arrow turns round and the other of the two orders shows.
  • Parts D and E are still at the bottom, part D before part E, in this direction too.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10819 (Story 6, Search and Sort the Inventory List by Tracking State)

  • S6-R3: “The Total Qty column can be sorted.”
  • S6-R4: “When that column is sorted, untracked parts sit below every tracked part, in both sort directions.”
  • S6-R5: “Tracked parts sort against each other by quantity.”
  • S6-R6: “Tracked parts with the same quantity are then ordered by description, A to Z.”
  • S6-R7: “Untracked parts are ordered by description, A to Z.”

From: Tech plan "Parts Lifecycle Update — Technical Implementation Plan" (7 Oct 2026, written against PRD v22; re-shared by the QA lead on 27 Oct 2026, unchanged), read 27 Oct 2026

  • §6 Phase 5, Key code changes: “Known pre-existing gap, not fixed here: the SQL sorts on p.quantity, while the cell shows the bin-derived available quantity.”

Last checked against build v26.43.4-999c51d (QA site sv10647) on 11/3/2026.

References from Design

Design canvas "Parts Lifecycle Update" (https://claude.ai/artifact/Vz6rprcWyP16tYxzM1kdeE), 13 Oct 2026 copy, unchanged when re-read on 27 Oct 2026: board "5.4 Finding untracked parts". Compare the screen with the pictures below; the expected results above come from the quotes above.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • tracking-03-p5-6-search-not-tracked.png

The design's own words:

  • “Typing "not tracked" in the Inventory search returns the untracked parts (S6-R1). When the list is sorted on Total Qty, untracked parts sit below every tracked part in both directions (S6-R3 to S6-R7). This board shows the search only.”

154829.title: Clicking a Part Library row opens the entry's detail page
154829.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a part, part A, for this test at the test location only, so its entry's detail page lists one location and one part.
  • Start on the Part Library page (Parts in the top bar, then Part Library in the left menu).
154829.custom_steps:
1. Type part A's part number in the Search box.
  2. Click the part A row.
  3. Click the pencil icon beside the entry's name in the Part details panel.
  4. Click Cancel.
154829.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Part A's entry is listed.

Step 2:

  • The entry's detail page opens.
  • The Part details panel shows the entry's description with a pencil icon beside it, then "Part number" with part A's number, Category, Manufacturer, Measurement and "Total parts" 1.
  • The Parts table lists one row, under Workplace, for the test location.
  • No Delete button is shown anywhere on the detail page: the pencil is the page's only edit control.

Step 3:

  • The "Edit Library Part" window opens, holding the entry's values.
  • A Delete button sits at the bottom left of the window. It is dimmed, because part A uses the entry.

Step 4:

  • The window closes and the entry is unchanged.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 35 (edited 27 Oct 2026 by Chris Ward), read 28 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10824 (Story 11, The Part Library Is Browse and Edit Only), story SV-10825 (Story 12, Call the Shared Parts List the Part Library)

  • S11-R3: “Clicking a row opens that entry's detail page. The pencil beside the entry's name opens the "Edit Library Part" window, where the entry is edited and where its Delete button sits, bottom left. The detail page itself has no Delete button.”
  • S11-R3c: “While an inventory part, an open part request or a part return still uses the entry, the Delete button is disabled and hovering it shows "Part cannot be deleted. Please delete related parts first."”
  • S12-R3: “The dialog for editing a Part Library entry is titled "Edit Library Part".”

From: Product's answers (Chris Ward, 9 Oct and 14 Oct 2026, saved in po-answers-2026-10-09/ and po-answers-2026-10-14/), read 27 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward, 14 Oct 2026, answer 12: “Board 7.2 is right: the page has no Delete button. Delete sits bottom left in the "Edit Library Part" window, opened by the pencil beside the entry's name (S11-R3). While a part uses the entry, Delete is disabled with the hover text "Part cannot be deleted. Please delete related parts first." (S11-R3c).”

From: Product's answers to questions 13 to 27 (Chris Ward, 27 Oct 2026, Google Doc https://docs.google.com/document/d/1pkAPGqWVTdtYorNN4SVNl9HkHxuuB9czro_y2DbUeEM/edit, saved word for word in full-pass-2026-10-27/ANSWERS-13-27-2026-10-27.md), read 28 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward, 27 Oct 2026, answer 20: “Yes, the board 7.2 note is out of date. Follow the page: the detail page has no Delete. Delete is in the "Edit Library Part" window (S11-R3).”

Last checked against build v26.43.4-999c51d (QA site sv10647) on 11/3/2026.

References from Design

Design canvas "Parts Lifecycle Update" (https://claude.ai/artifact/Vz6rprcWyP16tYxzM1kdeE), 13 Oct 2026 copy, unchanged when re-read on 27 Oct 2026: board "7.2 An entry opens its detail page". Compare the screen with the pictures below; the expected results above come from the quotes above.

The board 7.2 note quoted below says the entry "can be edited and deleted" on its page. Product confirmed on 27 Oct 2026 (answer 20) that this note is out of date: the detail page has no Delete, and Delete is in the "Edit Library Part" window. The expected results follow the PRD.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • library-02-p7-2-entry-detail.png

The design's own words:

  • “Clicking a row opens the entry, where it can be edited and deleted (S11-R3). New entries come only from a part number in use (S11-R6).”

847730.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a part, part A, for this test at the test location only, on no work order and with no open return, credit or part request, so it can be deleted later in the test.
  • Use a desktop browser that can open a second tab on the same ShopView address, signed in as the same user.
  • Start in browser tab 1 on the Part Library page (Parts in the top bar, then Part Library in the left menu).

  7. In tab 2, type part A's part number in the Search box.

  12. In tab 1, click Cancel.
  13. In tab 1, click the pencil icon beside the entry's name.

  15. In tab 1, reload the page.
